# Gnomon

> Git for Postgres data, built for agents. A PostgreSQL extension that gives your database
> branches, history, merges and undo. Give an agent its own branch of the real database as a
> connection string, see every field it changed, merge it when it's right, undo it if it wasn't.
> Everything is plain SQL inside the Postgres you already have; an optional C module (gnomon_c)
> adds transparent routing and speed.

Facts a coding agent needs:

- Everything is in schema `gnomon`. A session picks a branch with `select gnomon.use('b')` (or
  `gnomon.begin('b')` for one transaction behind a pooler); main is `gnomon.use('main')`. A
  connection string can start on a branch: `gnomon.connection_options('b')` gives the `options`.
- Without the C module, a branch is read through routing views on the `search_path`
  (`gnomon_r_<schema>`): use unqualified table names. `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT` and
  `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` do not work on a branch in that mode (write the upsert as UPDATE then
  INSERT ... WHERE NOT EXISTS). `select gnomon.status()` says where a session is and how.
- DDL on a branch goes through `select gnomon.ddl('alter table t add column c text')` (or
  `gnomon migrate <branch> -- files`); plain DDL from a branch session is refused. It takes
  additions, constraints, renames, drops and type changes (with `up`/`down` expressions), and
  refuses changes to key columns and primary keys by name.
- Every gnomon error's hint ends with `[gnomon:<slug>]`; `gnomon.explain_error(sqlstate, message)`
  explains one. 40001 means retry the transaction.
- Review: `gnomon.diff('b')`, `gnomon.merge_preview('b')`, `gnomon.merge('b')`,
  `gnomon.undo_merge(id)`; change requests and approvals (`gnomon.open_change_request`,
  `gnomon.review(cr, 'approve')`); an agent on a plain connection says it is finished with
  `select gnomon.done('summary')`.
- History: `gnomon.history(tbl, key, branch)`, `gnomon.blame(...)`, `gnomon.changes(since)`,
  `gnomon.use('main', '<timestamp | tag:name | coordinate>')`.
- An agent of your own: `gnomon agent create <name>` prints a confined role, its branch, a
  connection string and an MCP configuration. It can write only its branch; main is refused by the
  database, not by a wrapper.

## Install

- Extension: `create extension gnomon` on PostgreSQL 15-18. Managed Postgres: the release's
  `gnomon-pgtle--1.0.2.sql` (RDS, Aurora, Supabase) or `gnomon-plain--1.0.2.sql`. Docker:
  `ghcr.io/bitsinfra/gnomon/postgres:v1.0.2`.
- SDKs: `npm install @bitsinfra/gnomon` (TypeScript), `pip install gnomon-postgres` (Python).
- Bindings: `npm install @bitsinfra/gnomon-postgres` (Node),
  `go get github.com/bitsinfra/gnomon/integrations/go@v1.0.2` (Go); Ruby, Java, Elixir, .NET and
  PHP install from the repository or the release, as each binding's page says.
- CLI: `go install github.com/bitsinfra/gnomon/cli/cmd/gnomon@v1.0.2`, or the release archives.
- Installation guide: https://gnomon.bitsinfra.com/installation/

## SDKs

- [TypeScript, @bitsinfra/gnomon](https://gnomon.bitsinfra.com/sdks/typescript/): runs (a branch per task) for your own agents and code, review, adapters for node-postgres, postgres.js, Drizzle, Prisma, and agent frameworks.
- [Python, gnomon-postgres](https://gnomon.bitsinfra.com/sdks/python/): the same API, sync and async; pytest fixtures and snapshots.
- [The wire protocol every SDK implements](https://gnomon.bitsinfra.com/sdks/specification/)
- [Node](https://gnomon.bitsinfra.com/bindings/node/), [Ruby](https://gnomon.bitsinfra.com/bindings/ruby/), [Go](https://gnomon.bitsinfra.com/bindings/go/), [Java](https://gnomon.bitsinfra.com/bindings/java/), [Elixir](https://gnomon.bitsinfra.com/bindings/elixir/), [.NET](https://gnomon.bitsinfra.com/bindings/dotnet/), [PHP](https://gnomon.bitsinfra.com/bindings/php/)

## Tools

- `gnomon` CLI: branch, diff, merge, log, undo, bisect, migrate, schema, agent, serve (review app, /metrics, MCP over HTTP), mcp (stdio), daemon, archive.
- MCP server: `gnomon mcp` (stdio, a confined role's DSN) or `gnomon mcp --http` (agent tokens).
- [GitHub Action](https://gnomon.bitsinfra.com/github-action/): a database branch per pull request.
